summary: Victor Forte is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. from Temple University in 2004. By 2007, he was an assistant professor of religious studies at Albright College.

Victor H. Mair (1943–2026) studied at Dartmouth, the University of Washington, SOAS, and Harvard (Ph.D. c. 1976). A scholar of Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he taught at Harvard and became a professor at Penn in 1979.

Victor Henry (1850–1907) was a linguist and Indologist. He held positions at the University of Douai, École Centrale de Lille, and the University of Lille, before becoming professor of Sanskrit and comparative grammar at the University of Paris in 1888.

Victor Turner (1920–1983) studied at University College London and the University of Manchester (Ph.D. c. 1955). Active in religious studies, he held posts at Manchester, Cornell, the University of Chicago (1968–1977), and the University of Virginia (from 1977).
Victoria Sujata is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her Ph.D. at Harvard University, where she studied under Michael Aris.

Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya (1878–1954) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He served at Visva-Bharati University as a pandit and collation supervisor (attested 1929–1932) and later as Principal (1944), and was Asutosh Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta.

Vidya Dehejia studied at St. Xavier's College, Newnham College, and Cambridge (Ph.D. c. 1968). Working in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies, she held posts at the Smithsonian and at Columbia University, becoming Barbara Stoler Miller Professor in 2002.

Vidya Niwas Mishra (1926–2005) studied under Kshetresa Chandra Chattopadhyaya at Allahabad and at Gorakhpur University. A scholar of Indology and linguistics, he was Professor of Linguistics at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and vice-chancellor of Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.

Vilhelm Thomsen (1842–1927) studied at the University of Copenhagen (Ph.D. 1869). A scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he served as a professor at Copenhagen from 1887 to 1913 and became president of the Royal Danish Academy in 1909.
Vimalaraṁsi studied under Sayadaw U Silananda and Anagarika Munindra.

Vincenc Lesný (1882–1953) was an Indologist who studied at Charles University and its Faculty of Arts under Moriz Winternitz and Josef Zubatý. He subsequently held an academic post at Charles University from 1919 to 1953.

Vincent Arthur Smith (1848–1920) was a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist who studied at Trinity College Dublin. He served in the Indian Civil Service (1871–1900) and later held posts at St John's College and the University of Oxford (c. 1910–1920).

Vincent Breugem is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied at Taisho, Kyoto, and Hanazono Universities, and under Lucia Dolce. He earned his MA and PhD (2012) from Leiden University, where he was attested as a research fellow in 2012.

Vincent Eltschinger studied at Lausanne under Tom Tillemans and completed his habilitation at Vienna. A specialist in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, he was interim director at IKGA and became directeur d’études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études around 2015.

Vincent Goossaert is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied under Kristofer Schipper. He worked at the CNRS (1998–2012) and was appointed Professor of Daoist History at the École Pratique des Hautes Études around 2012.

Vincent Lefèvre works in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied under Bruno Dagens at the École Nationale des Chartes and Sorbonne Nouvelle University (habilitation 2007), and has served as a curator at the Musée Guimet.

Vincent Tournier is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Seishi Karashima and Cristina Scherrer-Schaub, earning a PhD from EPHE in 2012. He held an attested post at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient in 2021.
Vincenzo Vergiani is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Raffaele Torella and held a post at the University of Cambridge around 2008.

Virendra Nath Misra (1935–2015) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the University of Lucknow and Savitribai Phule Pune University. He served as Director of the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute from around 1993 to 2000.

Vishnu Sitaram Sukthankar (1887–1943) studied at Mumbai, Cambridge, Edinburgh, and Berlin under Heinrich Lüders, Hermann Jacobi, and Moriz Winternitz. An Indologist, he worked for the Archaeological Survey of India and became General Editor of the Mahabharata at BORI in 1925.
